A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe ResKoopNet. Their main text, equations, figures, references, and Appendices A.1–A.10 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original pendulum experiments, turbulent-flow analyses, and mouse neural-state clustering results, with additional comparisons and sensitivity analyses in the appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental and data-analysis results in Section 4 and the appendix.

M1.justification: The spectral-residual objective, alternating network/Koopman-matrix updates, dictionary components, and pseudospectrum procedure are unchanged. Algorithm 1 is renamed from NN-ResDMD to ResKoopNet without changing its steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nonlinear pendulum, two-dimensional airfoil turbulence, and Sensorium 2023 mouse visual-cortex state-partitioning tasks. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 4 retains EDMD, EDMD-DL, Hankel-DMD, and ResDMD. The neural comparison retains Hankel-DMD, EDMD with RBF basis, and Kernel-ResDMD; the appendix also retains the Hankel-DMD turbulence comparison.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain unchanged, including 90/240 pendulum initial conditions, 150-component turbulence preprocessing, neural dictionary sizes, and the MDS/UMAP/t-SNE and Davies-Bouldin evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The dictionary-size and architecture scans, Hankel-DMD mode analysis, mean-firing-rate comparisons, and alternative neural embeddings are retained. Figures 7–17 contain the same supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Repeated-run/seed information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. No confidence intervals, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests are newly reported.

E6.justification: The numerical and qualitative findings are unchanged, including the pendulum results with 300/350 observables, turbulence modes in Figure 5, and neural clustering comparisons. The underlying graphics in all result figures are identical across versions.

T1.justification: Assumption A.4(b) adds an unqualified strong-convexity requirement for J(theta). v3 assumed strong convexity only locally in the subsequent SGD discussion. The theorem, derivations, and convergence bounds remain unchanged, making this a limited strengthening of the stated assumptions.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that spectral-residual minimization addresses spectral inclusion, captures discrete and continuous spectra, and improves physical and biological analyses. The rewritten abstract and conclusion retain these claims and their scope.

C2.justification: The result interpretations and discussions of nonconvexity, computational cost, stochasticity, and architecture dependence are retained. The expanded conclusion repeats efficiency and stochastic-extension directions already discussed in v3 Appendix A.6.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, preprocessing details, and computational-cost information are unchanged. Appendix A.1 retains the same source-code link destination and future-availability statement; only the link's surrounding wording changes.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to EDMD, ResDMD, VAMPnets, and autoencoder approaches are retained. Reference changes concern numbering and bibliographic metadata, including publication details for the Sensorium retrospective.

P1.justification: v4 rewrites the abstract, portions of the neural-clustering discussion, and the conclusion. It also corrects Algorithm 1's name and makes scattered wording, affiliation, and bibliographic edits while retaining the section structure.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is reduced in size, mathematical displays are made more compact, and surrounding text and figure placement shift. All 17 figures retain their underlying graphics; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The clearer abstract and consistent Algorithm 1 name modestly improve readability, while Assumption A.4(b) makes a convergence premise more explicit. These gains are limited: the empirical evidence is unchanged, and the retained discussion of the practical loss's nonconvexity means the revised assumption does not resolve the convergence argument's applicability to the implemented network.
